newsitem.title: CHINA: Tough Thai measures good news for offshore bonds.
newsitem.headline: Tough Thai measures good news for offshore bonds.

text.p: Thai offshore bonds with longer maturities are likely to come back in favour on the back of Thailand's austerity measures, bankers said.

Thai finance minister Thanong Bidaya has announced a series of tough measures including the suspension of more than half of the country's 92 finance firms and tight monetary and fiscal policies such as cutting the current account deficit, raising the value added tax and controlling inflation.

"The IMF package is something that every body was waiting for...this is for the long-term good for the Kingdom's economic prospect," said Vincent Low, Fixed Income Strategist, Merrill Lynch (Singapore) Private Ltd.
The Kingdom of Thailand's outstanding 10-year yankee bond is currently consolidated at 101/106 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries, traders said.
The spread had widened to some 110 basis points before Thailand announced its rescue package.

While traders in Asia said they also expected some pick-up in demand for longer dated offshore bonds of Thai issuers, they did not expect shorter dated paper to perform well as tight policies cool off the economy in near term.
However, traders said they would not expect spreads to signficantly widen at the shorter end of the curve as current spreads have already factored in the news on tough economic measures.
Sovereign rated Bangkok Bank's outstanding floating rate debt issue, due in September 1999, is bid at 54 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
Last August, the bank launched a floating rate certificate of deposit issue that paid an all-in return of 24 basis points to the syndicate for an effective tenor of five years.
Thailand's foreign currency debt is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service and Single-A by Standard and Poor's Corp.
